item.description:
Fixes

  • Updates on a Mac where the app was downloaded with a browser: macOS keeps such an app in quarantine, which blocks Sparkle's installer for an app that isn't notarized ("An error occurred while running the updater"). Settings › General › Update now says so and gives the command to run once, with a button to copy it. The guide (installation, troubleshooting) explains it too.

Changes

  • Simpler Nearcast setup: Create a Group on one Mac, then Join a Group on the others, with a Paste button (a copied code is filled in automatically) and a share button (AirDrop, Messages…) for the code. Settings also show the connected Macs, a switch to pause Nearcast, and Leave Group. Errors are shown in place, not in an alert.

Fixes

  • The Settings button opens Settings on a first launch too: the app looked for Settings at a fixed place in its menu, which wasn't always right (upstream #175).
  • The tips shown when you put the app in the Dock or turn on "Discover more BLE devices" never appeared: macOS 27 blocks alerts opened at that moment.

Security

  • Nearcast v2: a new, more secure protocol (#41). Group IDs carry 130 bits of secret instead of about 48; everything in a message (sender, command, data) is encrypted and authenticated; old messages can't be replayed; the connection between Macs is encrypted, and only Macs that know the Group ID are let in; a Mac is no longer identified by its hardware UUID.
  • Breaking change: Nearcast v2 can't talk to earlier versions, the original AirBattery, or the AirBattery Mobile iOS app. Group IDs from before no longer work: Nearcast is turned off after the update, with a notification. Create a new Group ID and enter it on all your Macs.

Changes

  • Nearcast sends a Mac's data when it changes (or every 5 minutes) instead of at every refresh interval, and a Mac that joins gets the others' data right away.
  • The app declares its Nearcast network service to macOS, which recent versions need to find the other Macs.

Fixes

  • An iPhone or iPad plugged in shows the plug icon within a second, then the bolt once it reports charging: iOS reports a cable as connected right away, but as charging only 15 s to over a minute later, so the charging state took about a minute to appear in 1.13.1. A device plugged in over USB is also read again 10 s later, and a device attached over both USB and Wi-Fi is read over USB.

Fixes

  • An iPhone or iPad plugged in over USB is read right away, even if it was just read over Wi-Fi: its charging state shows up at once instead of up to a minute later.
  • A Bluetooth LE mouse or keyboard no longer keeps the generic Bluetooth icon when it was first read just as it reconnected (before macOS listed its type): its icon is corrected at the next read.

Fixes

  • iPhones, iPads and Apple Watches are read as soon as they show up, over USB or Wi-Fi: the app now listens to macOS's device service (usbmuxd) instead of checking every 15 s. An idle iPhone turns on its Wi-Fi only a few seconds at a time, and the 15 s check often missed it. Then, as before, they're read once per refresh interval while they stay. Measured over 6 minutes: the iPhone and Watch were read 5 times instead of about 1 or 2.

Performance

  • No more idevice_id launches every 15 s (about 480 per hour): measured over 6 minutes, 32 → 0. If the device service can't be reached, the app goes back to checking every 15 s.

Note

  • If you use Nearcast, macOS asks again for local network access after the update: allow it.

Performance

  • The Mac's battery is read when it changes (level, time left, charger, Low Power Mode, wake from sleep) instead of every second. The menu bar icon follows a charger plugged in or out right away. Measured over 3 minutes: idle wakeups went from about 30 per minute to 0 or 1.
  • Bluetooth accessories (Magic keyboards, mice and trackpads, and others) are read once per refresh interval (every minute by default, at most every 5 minutes) instead of every 24 s: their level moves by 1% in hours, and a newly connected accessory is still read right away. Measured over 6 minutes: system_profiler ran 10 times instead of 17.

Changes

  • Each read of an iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch is written to the system log, with its connection (USB or Wi-Fi), to see how often an idle iPhone is really read over Wi-Fi. See them in Console, or with log show --predicate 'subsystem == "io.github.msieurpafi.AirBattery" AND category == "idevice"'.

Note

  • After the update, macOS asks again for local network access: allow it.

Changes

  • No change to the app: this version checks that updates found and installed by the app itself work, from 1.11.0.

Note

  • After the update, macOS asks again for local network access: allow it.

Changes

  • In-app updates: AirBattery Plus finds and installs new versions itself, from this repository's releases (Sparkle, turned off since 1.7.0). On its second launch it asks whether to check automatically; Settings › General › Update and Check for Updates… are back. Updates are installed only if they carry the project's signature (its own key, not the original app's). The only internet access is this check, to GitHub: see Permissions & privacy.
  • Versions up to 1.10.0 can't update themselves: install this version by hand.

Note

  • After the update, macOS asks again for local network access: allow it.
